*   Alternatively, precompute the gradient magnitude volume to reduce runtime look-ups to 2 (data + precomputed gradient) [S2].

The claim states that precomputing the gradient magnitude volume reduces runtime look-ups to 2 (data + precomputed gradient). Source [S2] explicitly states: 'Of course the gradient can be precomputed, reducing the texture lookups to 2.' It also clarifies that standard computation requires 6 look-ups for the gradient, and since 1 lookup is needed for data, the total becomes 7. Precomputing the gradient allows the renderer to fetch the precomputed gradient value directly, resulting in 1 lookup for data and 1 lookup for the precomputed gradient volume, totaling 2 look-ups. Thus, the evidence fully supports the claim.

*   Allows isolation of boundaries that share similar scalar values [S4, book][S5, unofficial].

Both Source [S4] and Source [S5] explicitly state that 2D transfer functions (using data value and gradient magnitude) allow for the isolation of boundaries that share similar scalar values. [S4] notes that 1D transfer functions fail to render boundaries in isolation when they share data-value intervals, whereas 2D TFs resolve this by using gradient magnitude. [S5] provides a specific example where 1D TFs cannot distinguish dentin from background due to similar values, but 2D TFs can separate them.
